description: How the import pipeline (js/scripts/import-native-grammars.mjs) turns the rule names of an upstream grammar into readable English native rule names and concept records: the abbreviations and run-together keywords upstream names use with the words that replace them, and per grammar the names and concepts a reviewer decided by hand. Every entry is a reviewed merge decision; the merge report of each language lists where it applied.

words.reason: The C keyword _Alignas (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.7.5) run together.
The C operator _Alignof (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.5.3.4) gives the alignment of a type.
The asm keyword introduces inline assembly.
The C standard writes bit-field (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.7.2.1).
An abbreviation of character; the C type char holds a character.
The preprocessing directive #elif (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.10.1) is else if.
The preprocessing directive #elifdef (ISO/IEC 9899:2024 section 6.10.2) is else if defined.
The preprocessing directive #ifdef (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.10.1) is if defined.
An init-declarator (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.7) declares with an initializer.
The offsetof macro (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 7.19) run together.
The sizeof operator (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.5.3.4) run together.
The C standard calls a struct a structure (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.7.2.1).

grammar.preprocessor-argument.reason: A preprocessor argument is the text after a directive or a macro name, while the preprocessor parameters are the names a function-like macro declares.

grammar.argument-list.reason: An argument list gives the values a call passes, while a parameter list declares the names a function takes.
